papers.title: Capacity-controlled EEG denoising: diminishing reconstruction returns on semi-synthetic benchmarks and task-dependent downstream utility.
papers.summary: A capacity-controlled EEG denoising study evaluated a depthwise-separable convolutional denoiser (1.05K–40.26K parameters) on semi-synthetic benchmarks and downstream tasks, finding that reconstruction fidelity improvements with capacity depend on metric and dataset, and that denoising often reduced downstream classification accuracy (e.g., CSP+LDA accuracy decreased for EOG, EMG, and mixed contamination on IV-2a).

papers.title: Preprocessing and feature extraction co-optimization for low-power EEG-based neurodegenerative disease detection: a benchmark on STM32 embedded platforms.
papers.summary: A lightweight TinyML framework for embedded EEG classification on STM32 microcontrollers was benchmarked using 12 preprocessing techniques and 6 classifiers on two OpenNeuro datasets (88 participants), with Sparse Decomposition combined with XGBoost achieving the best performance (94.46% accuracy, 92.1% sensitivity) while requiring only 45 KB SRAM.

papers.title: Feature processing for single-trial semantic decoding from EEG: a factorial comparison with pre-registered replication
papers.summary: A factorial comparison of 640 feature-processing configurations for single-trial EEG semantic decoding across three tasks showed that signal representation had the largest effect: waveform features achieved 56.6% balanced accuracy versus 50.6% for theta-band power, and adding band power to waveform reduced accuracy by 1.8 percentage points; these effects replicated and were larger in a pre-registered study of 283 new participants.

papers.title: A post-training quantization framework for EEG-based sleep stage classification.
papers.summary: A post-training quantization framework for EEG-based sleep stage classification was proposed, using layer-wise sensitivity-based thresholds and dynamic low-rank compensation to compress models to 4 bits, achieving near-lossless accuracy (drop <1%) while reducing model size by nearly 8x across Sleep-EDF-20, Sleep-EDF-78, and SHHS datasets.

papers.title: Sleep as a window into thalamocortical pathology: generative modeling implicates NMDA receptor hypofunction in 22q11.2 deletion syndrome.
authors: Marianne B M van den Bree
papers.summary: Using a conductance-based thalamocortical Dynamic Causal Model on sleep EEG from children with 22q11.2 deletion syndrome and neurotypical siblings, the study found that increasing NMDA receptor efficacy produced the strongest alignment with sibling spectra, implicating NMDA receptor hypofunction as a key mechanism in 22q11.2DS.

papers.title: Integrating convolutional variational autoencoders and the Gaussian mixture model for efficient manifold learning and clustering of spatially preserved EEG topographic maps.
papers.summary: The authors developed Conv-VaDE, a convolutional variational deep embedding model with a Gaussian mixture prior for clustering spatially preserved EEG topographic maps into microstates, and on LEMON resting-state data it produced a reproducible latent manifold (silhouette 0.232) with probabilistic soft assignments and decodable cluster centers, while modified k-means retained higher silhouette and 4-5 percentage points higher global explained variance.

papers.title: Before synchrony: the unresolved specificity of neural oscillations across brains.
papers.summary: A commentary arguing that EEG hyperscanning research should move beyond descriptive inter-brain synchrony reports by accounting for 1/f aperiodic activity and transient oscillatory bursts, and should formulate mechanistically grounded hypotheses specifying why synchrony is expected in particular frequencies and regions.

papers.title: Transcranial temporal interference stimulation increases slow waves during human NREM sleep
papers.summary: In 32 participants receiving 1 Hz transcranial temporal interference stimulation (tTIS) and 11 carrier-only controls during NREM sleep, tTIS increased slow-wave density by about 20% during and 30% after stimulation, and stronger modeled electric fields were associated with greater shifts toward N3 sleep.

papers.title: Simultaneous Two-Photon Calcium Imaging, Electroencephalography, and Electromyography with Intracortical Electrical Stimulation in Freely Moving Mice.
papers.summary: Describes a protocol integrating two-photon calcium imaging, intracortical electrical stimulation, EEG, and EMG in freely moving tethered mice using a stable chronic cranial-window/electrode implant, with the retrosplenial cortex as target. The preparation yields cellular-resolution calcium signals with concurrent electrophysiological and motor-state measures and supports stimulation-aligned response analysis.

papers.title: Noise resilience in brain decoding driven by spiking neural networks for responsive robot control.
papers.summary: Benchmarked shallow CNN and LIF/adaptive-LIF spiking neural networks for four-class EEG motor imagery decoding on the BNCI 2014-001 dataset and integrated the spiking model into a decoding-to-robot-control pipeline. Spiking models were far more noise-robust than the CNN: under global Gaussian noise CNN accuracy dropped 58.56% versus 0.80% for adaptive LIF, and with one electrode removed CNN lost 36.00% versus 0.34%.

papers.title: EEG Decoding in Context: A Framework for Tuning-Free EEG Foundation Models
papers.summary: Introduces a tuning-free EEG foundation-model framework using in-context learning with EEG-specific context construction, a frozen in-context predictor, and metric-based context adaptation, requiring no parameter updates or validation-driven model selection. Across ten datasets spanning seven EEG decoding paradigms it achieved the highest mean balanced accuracy among eleven specialized and fine-tuned baselines.

papers.title: Bayesian Complete-Pooling in Cross-Subject Classification for Motor Imagery Electroencephalogram.
papers.summary: Compared Bayesian complete-pooling classifiers against matched frequentist pipelines for cross-subject left- versus right-hand motor imagery EEG across 20 datasets, using Brier score decomposition, AUC, and entropy with random-effects meta-analysis. Bayesian models significantly improved reliability and increased predictive uncertainty, but these effects disappeared when flagged posterior-sampling datasets were excluded, and Bayesian pipelines consumed roughly 13 times more energy.

papers.title: Condition-associated EEG signatures in N-back tasks: temporal dynamics, classification, and generalization.
papers.summary: Examined condition-associated EEG signatures in 15 healthy adults performing N-back level (1/2/3-back) and stimulus-pacing manipulations with an 8-channel setup, analyzing bandpower, workload indices, N2/P3b ERPs, and classifier generalization. P3b amplitude decreased with higher load and faster pacing; N-SPEED three-class decoding generalized more consistently than N-LEVELS, but cross-paradigm transfer did not survive correction and decoding was constrained by small sample and deterministic block order.

papers.title: CFCR-Net: cross-frequency connectivity reorganization learning for EEG-based driver fatigue detection.
papers.journal: Computer methods in biomechanics and biomedical engineering
papers.summary: Proposes CFCR-Net, a cross-frequency connectivity reorganization learning framework that couples wavelet packet sub-band decomposition with adaptive cross-frequency graph learning for EEG-based driver fatigue detection. On SEED-VIG it achieved 0.8831 accuracy, 0.9102 F1-score, and 75.2% cross-subject accuracy, with visualization showing fatigue-related connectivity reorganizing toward low-frequency dominance.

papers.title: A Neuro-Inspired Dual-Pathway Attention Network for EEG-Based Identity Recognition.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: The authors propose a dual-pathway attention network for EEG-based identity recognition that separates bottom-up perceptual feature extraction from top-down prior-guided modulation, fused by a quality-aware gate based on instantaneous signal stability. The method achieved 93.8% accuracy on DEAP (5.3 percentage points above the best baseline) and 97.2% on THU-EP, with only 2.5% and 5.2% performance drops in cross-session tests on noisy SEED-IV and 76.8% accuracy with only 1% of training data on THU-EP.

papers.title: PRISM-MP: Psychology-guided and reliability-aware multimodal learning for cross-musician emotion recognition during musical performance.
papers.summary: Presents PRISM-MP, a psychology-guided, reliability-aware multimodal framework combining EEG, ECG, and audio for cross-musician emotion recognition during musical performance, evaluated on 11 musicians under leave-one-musician-out testing. It reported 92.14% accuracy, 91.82% balanced accuracy, macro-F1 0.910, MCC 0.892, and calibration error 0.041, with robustness to missing ECG/audio and partial EEG channel loss.

papers.title: Hypothalamic orexin input to the medial amygdala promotes arousal from anaesthesia and modulates exploratory behaviour.
papers.summary: Using viral tracing, electrophysiology, optogenetics, EEG/EMG, and fibre photometry in male orexin-Cre mice, the study defined a lateral hypothalamic orexin projection to the medial amygdala and showed that its optogenetic activation promoted arousal from isoflurane anaesthesia, delayed induction, accelerated emergence, and suppressed open-field exploration. Medial amygdala vesicular GABA transporter (MeAvGAT) neurons acted as a key downstream target, replicating arousal-promoting and reduced exploratory effects.

papers.title: Time-dependent alterations of the heart-brain axis in rats following a single microwave exposure.
papers.summary: Investigated time-dependent heart-brain axis alterations in male Wistar rats after a single S-band microwave exposure (2.856 GHz, 50 mW/cm², 30 min), finding autonomic imbalance, heart rate variability and ECG/EEG abnormalities, and injury markers peaking on Day 3, with synchronized molecular remodeling in myocardium (cytochrome P450 detoxification, Adh6, Cyp4f5) and hippocampus (neuroactive ligand-receptor signaling, Adra2b, Chrna3).

papers.title: Propofol rapidly reverses cognitive impairments with restoration of sleep stability and alleviation of neuroinflammation in sleep-deprived mice.
papers.summary: Shows that a single subanesthetic bolus of propofol rapidly ameliorated acute total sleep deprivation-induced cognitive impairments in mice, with effects from one hour and persisting 24 hours in Y-maze, novel object recognition, and object location tasks, whereas zolpidem was ineffective. Propofol restored NREM sleep stability, upregulated BMAL1, reduced IL-1β and TNF-α, and restored BDNF, PSD-95, SYN, and hippocampal dendritic spines.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-enabled quality assurance for point-of-care electroencephalographic cap placement by inexperienced users.
papers.summary: In a prospective randomized crossover validation study with 30 participants and 60 placement trials, the authors developed and tested an AI-enabled tool for quality assurance of EEG cap placement by inexperienced users compared with expert technologist placement. Mean absolute positioning error was 0.938 cm with app guidance versus 0.855 cm with expert placement, demonstrating noninferiority against a prespecified 0.5-cm margin, with clinically acceptable placement achieved in 93.3% of app-guided versus 100% of expert trials.

papers.title: Performance evaluation of smart ring-derived sleep parameters compared with portable electroencephalography in university students.
papers.summary: Compared sleep parameters from the SOXAI smart ring against portable EEG in 49 university students during habitual home sleep, finding strong correlation for total sleep time (ρ=0.70) but underestimation of TST and light sleep, overestimation of WASO and deep sleep, limited wake detection specificity, and only 50.0% four-stage classification accuracy (κ=0.27).

papers.title: Generalizable mapping of the Epileptogenic Zone from interictal Intracranial EEG using an implant topology-aware Transformer
papers.summary: Developed an implant topology-aware transformer that combines interictal intracranial EEG features with electrode coordinates to map the epileptogenic zone, trained on 476 patients from three public datasets and tested on 216 patients from five independent centers, achieving median AUPRC 0.71 and AUROC 0.92 in Engel I patients and outperforming spike-rate and seizure-onset-zone baselines.

papers.title: EEG Source Localization with High-Resolution 40-Tissue Head Models: A Comparative Study with MEG during Photic Driving
papers.summary: The authors present a pipeline using the boundary element fast multipole method to compute EEG leadfields on high-resolution 40-tissue head models and applied it to six participants during photic driving, comparing 61-channel EEG source localizations from 40-tissue and 5-layer models with each other and with simultaneously recorded MEG. The two models produced highly consistent EEG source localizations (weighted relative difference below 3%), both in close agreement with MEG localizations within the visual cortex, establishing 40-tissue models as a practical and robust basis for EEG source localization.

papers.title: Hybrid coati-gozde optimization-based EEG channel selection for automated alcoholism detection.
papers.journal: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine
papers.summary: Proposed a hybrid COA-GOZDE optimization algorithm for EEG channel selection using EEMD-derived IMF statistical features and kNN, Random Forest, and MLP classifiers, achieving 94.6% alcoholism detection accuracy with only 14 of 61 channels (79.34% channel reduction) and outperforming GWO, HHO, WOA, and COA.

papers.title: Preparatory beta activity reflects the precision demands of an upcoming movement
papers.summary: EEG recorded in 27 healthy adults preparing reaches to narrow versus wide targets showed lower preparatory beta power (13–30 Hz) over bilateral parieto-occipital electrodes for narrow, higher-precision targets, with no alpha or theta differences. Narrow targets also produced more precise movements, greater muscle co-activation, and larger long-latency perturbation responses, indicating preparatory beta reflects task precision demands.

papers.title: NeuroMotion: Aligning EEG to Discrete Motion Primitives for Continuous Motion Decoding
papers.summary: Presented NeuroMotion, a framework that aligns EEG representations to VQ-discretized motion primitives and uses an E2M Transformer with contrastive alignment and geometric refinement for continuous motion decoding across full-body, lower-limb, and upper-limb paradigms, achieving the best mean reconstruction performance among baselines on all three datasets under a last-session test protocol.

papers.title: Learning Neurovascular Codes for EEG-to-fMRI Synthesis
papers.summary: Introduced Neurovascular Codes as shared EEG representations for fMRI synthesis, training target-specific EEG encoders whose concatenated features condition a stochastic interpolant generator, and reported 19.1% and 19.8% average Pearson correlation improvements over the strongest encoder baselines in within-subject and held-out-subject evaluation across eight public simultaneous EEG-fMRI datasets.

papers.title: Interrater agreement of seizure onset and spread in scalp EEG
papers.summary: Three epileptologists independently annotated onset and contralateral spread channels and timing for 79 seizures from 48 presurgical patients, yielding substantial onset laterality agreement (Gwet k=0.73) and comparable spread-presence agreement (0.63), but lower channel-level agreement for spread (Cohen k=0.38) versus onset (0.57). The authors release a multi-expert annotated dataset as a reference standard for automated spread detection.

papers.title: Shared Neural Dynamics of Sentence-Level Language Processing in Verbally Proficient Autistic and Non-Autistic Adults
papers.summary: Using EEG during rapid serial visual presentation of sentences and pseudoword lists, the authors compared verbally proficient autistic and non-autistic adults and found comparable oscillatory responses across theta, alpha, beta, and gamma bands, with beta-band activity increasing over sentence position and correlating with verbal ability. The results indicate largely shared neural dynamics of sentence-level language processing in both groups.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in epilepsy care: a systematic review and meta-analysis of clinical applications in diagnosis, classification, outcome prediction, and surgical decision-making.
papers.summary: This PRISMA-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis pooled 102 studies of AI/ML in epilepsy and found strong discriminative performance across clinical tasks, with the highest pooled AUC for etiological classification (0.929), followed by diagnosis (0.899), surgical referral (0.895), and outcome prediction (0.807), alongside high risk of bias and scarce external validation. Sensitivity was lowest for surgical referral (0.729), highlighting a clinically relevant asymmetry.

papers.title: Machine learning-based identification of a psychotherapy-predictive electroencephalographic signature in PTSD.
papers.summary: Using high-density resting-state EEG from military veterans with PTSD, the authors developed a machine-learning treatment-predictive signature that generalized across prolonged exposure and cognitive processing therapy; the signature was dominated by theta-frequency connectivity differences and identified a putative psychotherapy-resistant subgroup.

papers.title: Implementation of nurse-led frontal electroencephalography for early neurological assessment in patients after cardiac arrest: the FRONT study.
papers.summary: In a type 3 hybrid implementation study, ICU nurses were trained to apply a 6-electrode frontal EEG within 3 h of ICU admission after cardiac arrest; fEEG was applied in 88% of patients (73% within 3 h), with correct electrode placement and improved nurse perceptions, though diagnostic and prognostic value remain untested.

papers.title: Fluorescence spectroscopy coupled with dual-modal cross-attention feature fusion for accurate quantification of microplastics in agricultural soils.
papers.summary: The authors developed a fluorescence spectroscopy dual-modal cross-attention feature fusion (DM-CAFF) framework, combining 2D GAF image transforms and VAE-based augmentation, for quantifying microplastics in agricultural soils; it achieved R2p of 0.9757 and RMSEp of 0.4437 wt% and classified seven microplastic categories.

papers.title: A Mesohydrous Metallic Gel for Imperceptible Electrophysiology.
papers.summary: Inspired by the stratum corneum's mesohydrous state, the authors report a silver-nanowire-reinforced mesohydrous metallic gel (MSC) with >10^6 S m-1 conductivity, sub-micron thickness and dual electronic/ionic conduction that enables imperceptible skin electrophysiology and neuromuscular stimulation.

papers.title: Impact of EEG-related HPO terms on phenotype-driven variant prioritization in pediatric epilepsy.
papers.summary: Across 33 pediatric epilepsy patients, three HPO profiles differing in EEG terms were compared for phenotype-driven variant prioritization; more specific EEG-related HPO terms were associated with lower phenotype and Exomiser scores and changed the top-ranked gene in 24-55% of patients, while the full profile produced the shortest candidate lists.

papers.title: Machine learning-assisted fusion of urinary Raman and fluorescence spectra for detection of urothelial carcinoma.
papers.journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
papers.summary: Combined fiber-optic Raman and UV/VIS-excited fluorescence spectroscopy of unprocessed urine with machine learning to detect urothelial carcinoma in 285 patients (120 cases, 165 controls). A PCA-LDA fusion model reached only ~64% accuracy, whereas an artificial neural network on full spectral data with augmentation exceeded 90% accuracy.

papers.title: Beyond Patching: Consistent Circuit Discovery via Gradient Spectral Analysis
papers.summary: Proposes Spectral Circuit Analysis (SCA), a counterfactual-free, gradient-spectral SVD pipeline that discovers circuits consistently across paraphrased inputs without task-specific prompt pairs. On twelve circuit-discovery tasks in GPT-2 Small and Pythia-160M, SCA matches or exceeds EAP-family methods and recovers IOI canonical heads with Precision@K = 1.0 in top-10 slices on GPT-2 Small.

papers.title: An apparently de novo UBE3A missense variant p.(Tyr777Cys) in the HECT domain in a child with an atypical early childhood phenotype suggestive of Angelman syndrome: a case report and focused literature review.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 30-month-old boy with global developmental delay, severe expressive language impairment, EEG abnormalities, and delayed myelination who carries an apparently de novo UBE3A HECT-domain missense variant p.(Tyr777Cys) classified as a variant of uncertain significance, with a focused literature review.

papers.title: JAK Inhibition in Febrile Infection-Related Epilepsy Syndrome: A Case Series from Sydney Children's Hospital.
papers.summary: This case series reports three paediatric FIRES patients treated with the JAK1/2 inhibitor baricitinib alongside immunotherapy, with EEG normalization or improvement and clinically meaningful seizure reduction observed in the patients, although one patient ultimately died.

papers.title: Emergence of ANTI-GAD65 Autoimmunity in Longstanding Drug-Resistant Temporal Lobe Epilepsy.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 29-year-old woman with longstanding drug-resistant temporal lobe epilepsy in whom high-titre serum and CSF anti-GAD65 antibodies were detected during epilepsy surgery workup, followed by marked seizure reduction after corticosteroids, IVIG, rituximab, and mycophenolate mofetil.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
